q: 1. The art of representation of an object by systemic lines on a paper is known as
explain: Drawing is the technical method of representing an object's shape and features using lines on a flat surface.

q: 2. Drawing is the ................of engineers.
explain: Engineering drawing is considered the universal language of engineers because it conveys technical information across different regions and languages without ambiguity.

q: 3. The edge of drawing board where T-square is made to slide is called
explain: The working edge (or ebony edge) is a perfectly straight wooden strip on the left side of the drawing board used to guide the T-square.

q: 4. As per ISI recommended size of drawing board is/are
explain: ISI (Indian Standards Institution) specifies these standard sizes for drawing boards to ensure uniformity in technical drawings.

q: 5. Working edge of drawing board is kept ........... of the user.
explain: For right-handed users, the ebony/working edge is always on the left so the T-square can be manipulated by the left hand while drawing with the right.

q: 6. Drawing board is made of
explain: Softwood like white pine or fir is used because it allows drawing pins to be inserted and removed easily, and 'seasoning' prevents warping.

q: 7. During drawing stock of T-square is placed
options: adjoining the working edge of the board
adjoining the sliding edge of the board
explain: The 'stock' is the cross-head of the T-square that must be held firmly against the working edge of the board to ensure horizontal lines are parallel.

q: 8. The working edge of T-square is used to
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square serves multiple purposes: drawing horizontal lines, ensuring they are parallel, and providing a base for set squares to draw vertical or inclined lines.

q: 9. Set squares are not used to draw
explain: Horizontal lines are primarily drawn using the T-square or a mini-drafter; set squares are typically used for vertical and inclined lines relative to the T-square.

q: 10. The diameter of semi-circle is called
explain: The flat bottom edge of a semi-circular protractor, which aligns with the $0^{\circ}-180^{\circ}$ line, is referred to as its base.

q: 11. Drawing pins/cello tapes are used to
explain: These items are essential for securing the drawing sheet to the board to prevent it from shifting during work.

q: 12. When only one drawing is to be made then its position should be
explain: Placing a single drawing in the center of the sheet ensures proper balance, aesthetic appeal, and space for annotations/dimensions on all sides.

q: 13. Working/ drawing space on the paper is determined by
explain: Border lines are drawn on the sheet to define the actual area available for the technical drawing and to provide a frame for the work.

q: 14. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called
explain: This is a repetition of Q3; the working edge is the guide for the T-square's vertical movement.

q: 15. To prevent warping of the board ........are cleated at its back.
explain: Battens are wooden strips fixed to the back of the board to prevent it from bending or warping due to moisture or temperature changes.

q: 16. The two parts of T-square are........ and .......
explain: A T-square consists of a 'stock' (the head) and a 'blade' (the long straight edge) joined at a $90^{\circ}$ angle.

q: 17. Angles in multiples of 15 degrees are constructed by the combined use of
explain: By combining $45^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}/60^{\circ}$ set squares on a T-square base, one can achieve angles like $15^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$, $105^{\circ}$, etc.

q: 18. To draw or measure angles ........... is used.
explain: A protractor is specifically designed with degree graduations to measure and mark angles accurately.

q: 19. For drawing large-size circles .................. is attached to the compass (>150mm).
explain: A lengthening bar is an extension that increases the radius of the compass beyond its standard limit.

q: 20. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: Bow compasses are rigid and small, making them ideal for maintaining precision while drawing small circles.

q: 21. The scale should never be used as a ......... for drawing straight lines.
explain: Using a measuring scale as a straight edge for drawing can damage its precision graduations; a dedicated straight edge should be used instead.

q: 22. Measurements from scale to the drawing are transferred with the aid of
explain: Dividers are used to pick up a measurement from a scale and transfer it to the drawing sheet without marking the scale.

q: 23. .......... is used for setting of short equal distances.
explain: Bow dividers are used for repeating small, equal measurements along a line accurately.

q: 24. In drafting machine, which one does not follow
explain: A drafting machine (mini-drafter) combines the functions of a T-square, set squares, and protractor, but has nothing to do with leveling equipment.

q: 25. Which one is not drafting equipment?
explain: All listed items (drafter, scale, and even a dust cloth to keep the sheet clean) are considered part of the drafting environment.

q: 26. Circles of very small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: A drop compass is specifically used for very tiny circles, where the center point remains fixed while the pencil lead 'drops' and rotates around it.

q: 27. .............is used to protect the adjoining lines on the drawing when some parts of the line is being erased.
explain: An erasing shield is a thin metal or plastic plate with holes of various shapes that allows erasing a specific area without disturbing nearby lines.

q: 28. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of -
explain: A chisel edge is used for drawing long, thin, uniform lines (like outlines) because the wide edge wears down more slowly than a point.

q: 29. Pencil of ......grade sharpened in the form of ........ is used for sketching.
explain: Sketching requires a softer lead (like HB or B) and a conical point to allow for free-hand movement and varied line weight.

q: 30. ......... is used for drawing curves which can't be drawn by a compass
explain: French curves are templates with various irregular radii used to draw smooth, non-circular curves.

q: 31. To remove unnecessary lines ....... is used
explain: The standard tool for correcting errors or removing construction lines is an eraser.

q: 32. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the
explain: A drafting machine (or mini-drafter) is an all-in-one tool that replaces several individual drafting instruments.

q: 33. Circle and arcs of circles are drawn by means of a .......
explain: A compass is the primary instrument used for drawing circular geometry.

q: 34. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called
explain: In technical drawing, the 'Plan' view is the top-down projection onto the horizontal plane.

q: 35. Inking pen is used for drawing ----------- in ink
explain: While technical pens can be used for many things, traditional inking pens were primarily used with guides to draw permanent straight lines.

q: 36. Set squares are used for drawing ......., ......... and .......... lines.
explain: Set squares are versatile tools used to draw vertical lines, standard angles (30, 45, 60), and parallel lines when slid along a reference.

q: 37. The purpose of making the drawing board with seasoned soft wood
options: for fixing of drawing paper with the help of drawing pin
explain: Softwood is essential so that drawing pins can penetrate the surface easily without damaging the board or the pins.

q: 38. For dimensioning and lettering normally following pencils are used
explain: H is used for thin, precise dimension lines, and HB is used for lettering to make it clear and legible.

q: 39. The most important material for drawing is
explain: Without paper and a marking tool (pencil), no drawing can be created; they are the fundamental necessities.

q: 40. Which pencil is used for thinner line ?
explain: The 'H' stands for Hardness. Higher numbers (like 2H) have harder lead, which produces thinner, lighter lines.

q: 41. 9H pencil is ......than the 7H pencil
explain: In the pencil grading system, 9H is the hardest grade available, making it harder than 7H.

q: 42. To draw very light line which pencil is used
explain: Harder pencils (like 2H) do not deposit much graphite, resulting in very light construction lines.

q: 43. The paper size of A3 is
explain: Standard ISO paper sizes: A3 is 297mm x 420mm (double the size of A4).

q: 44. Size of A4 size paper is
explain: A4 is the most common paper size, measuring exactly 210mm by 297mm.

q: 45. Number of equal pieces of A4 size paper from A0 is equal to
explain: Each step in the A-series halves the area. $A0 \rightarrow A1 \rightarrow A2 \rightarrow A3 \rightarrow A4$. That is $2^4 = 16$ sheets.

q: 46. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A1 (drawing sheet).
explain: One A0 sheet is equivalent to two A1 sheets placed side-by-side.

q: 47. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A2 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^2$), A0 is four times the size of A2.

q: 48. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A3 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^3$), A0 is eight times the size of A3.

q: 49. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A4 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^4$), A0 is sixteen times the size of A4.

q: 50. The equipment mainly used to transfer the measurements is
explain: Dividers have two sharp points specifically intended to pick up distances from a scale and transfer them to the work without marking the original source.

q: 51. The shape of scales are
explain: Drafting scales are commonly manufactured in flat shapes for portability or triangular shapes to provide multiple scale ratios on a single instrument.

q: 52. The drawing for municipality is done at scale
explain: Municipal drawings often use 1:100 (metric) or 1" = 8' (FPS) as standard scales for site plans and building layouts to ensure clarity for legal approvals.

q: 53. To measure a fraction we use
explain: A diagonal scale is used to represent three consecutive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, and centimeters) and can measure very small fractions of a unit.

q: 54. Find the RF for scale 1cm = 25 km
explain: RF = Drawing Distance / Actual Distance. $1\text{ cm} / (25 \times 1000 \times 100)\text{ cm} = 1 / 2,500,000$.

q: 55. Tracing paper is also named as
explain: Vellum is a high-quality, translucent paper specifically designed for tracing and manual drafting.

q: 56. During draw a drawing we start from
options: top to bottom of drawing paper
bottom to top of drawing paper
right to left of drawing paper
left to right of drawing paper
explain: Drawing from top-to-bottom and left-to-right (for right-handed users) prevents the hand or tools from smudging lines that were already drawn.

q: 57. Bisecting a line means, divide a line into..... equal part.
explain: To 'bisect' literally means to cut into two equal portions.

q: 58. The angle between two perpendicular line is
explain: Perpendicular lines are defined as lines that intersect at a right angle ($90^{\circ}$).

q: 59. The angle between two horizontal line is
explain: Two parallel horizontal lines have a $0^{\circ}$ angle between them, while a single continuous horizontal line represents a $180^{\circ}$ straight angle.

q: 60. Dashed (dotted) line is used for indication
explain: Dashed lines represent features that are not visible from the current point of view but exist within or behind the object.

q: 61. The lines which are drawn to represent visible edges and surface boundaries of objects are called ............
explain: Visible edges are represented by continuous thick lines known as object lines, outlines, or principal lines.

q: 62. The unseen/inner edge of an object is represented by
explain: Similar to hidden lines, these are represented by short dashes (often referred to as 'dotted' in older textbooks).

q: 63. The space between two sentences should be left equal to
explain: For legibility in technical lettering, spacing between sentences is typically twice the height of the letters used.

q: 64. In case of aligned method of dimensioning, they can be readable form
options: bottoms and right side of drawing sheet
bottoms and left side of drawing sheet
bottoms and top side of drawing sheet
explain: In the aligned system, dimensions are placed perpendicular to the dimension line and read from the bottom or the right side of the sheet.

q: 65. In case of unidirectional method of dimensioning, they can be read from
options: bottom side of drawing sheet only
right side of drawing sheet only
top side of drawing sheet only
left side of drawing sheet only
explain: Unidirectional dimensioning keeps all text horizontal, regardless of the line's direction, so they are always read from the bottom.

q: 66. The main objective of writing letters/alphabets on the drawing is to make the drawing
explain: Lettering provides vital non-graphical information such as titles, materials, notes, and specific measurements.

q: 67. The angle between isometric axes is
explain: In isometric projection, the three principal axes are spaced equally at $120^{\circ}$ to each other.

q: 68. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is
explain: Due to the tilt of the object in isometric projection, all lines are foreshortened to approximately 81.5% of their true length.

q: 69. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by
explain: Isometric Length = $True Length \times \cos(30^{\circ}) / \cos(45^{\circ}) \approx 0.815 \times True Length$.

q: 70. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed
options: out side of eye towards eye
explain: The picture plane is the transparent 'window' situated between the observer's eye and the object being viewed.

q: 71. Perspective projection is used to represent
explain: Perspective mimics how the human eye sees the world, with distant objects appearing smaller, providing a naturalistic 3D view.

q: 72. Normally perspective projection is used by ....... to represent the object
explain: Manufacturers and architects use perspective for marketing and presentations because it is easy for non-technical clients to understand.

q: 73. Picture plane is
explain: The theoretical picture plane must be transparent so the projectors from the object can pass through it to the eye.

q: 74. The plane on which perspective is formed is called:
explain: The image (perspective) is mathematically projected onto the Picture Plane (PP).

q: 75. Ground plane is
explain: The ground plane is the horizontal surface on which the object and the observer are assumed to stand.

q: 76. Perspective drawing is done for
explain: While engineers use orthographic for construction, perspective is used extensively for marketing and product visualization.

q: 77. Why perspective drawing is done by manufacturer?
options: It is easy to express in the market
explain: Its primary benefit for manufacturers is that it presents the product in a visually appealing, realistic manner.

q: 78. In orthographic projection which one have all three views same
explain: A cube looks like a square from all principal sides, and a sphere looks like a circle from every direction.

q: 79. Which is not pictorial projection?
explain: Pictorial projections (Isometric, Oblique, Perspective) show 3D views; trigonometric is a mathematical field, not a projection type.

q: 80. View of circle in orthographic is
explain: A circle appears as a circle if parallel to the plane, but as an ellipse or a line if inclined to the plane.

q: 81. In orthographic projection, projector lines are
explain: Projectors in orthographic projection are parallel to each other and perpendicular (vertical) to the plane of projection.

q: 82. In third angle projection top view is put
explain: In Third Angle Projection, the observer 'looks through' the plane, so the Top View is placed above the Front View.

q: 83. In case of third angle projection, plan is kept at
explain: Note: Plan (Top View) is above Front View, but some contexts refer to the position relative to the ground line. Based on standard key: 'below'.

q: 84. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: There are 6 principal views: Front, Top, Bottom, Right-side, Left-side, and Rear.

q: 85. Mechanical lines are types of
options: line of drawn with free hand
explain: Mechanical lines refer to precise lines created using instruments like scales and T-squares rather than free-hand sketching.

q: 86. The main purpose of leader line is
options: to connect a note with the feature
explain: Leader lines are thin lines used to point to a specific part of a drawing to provide descriptions or dimensions.

q: 87. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45 degree with
explain: Hatching (section lines) should be drawn at $45^{\circ}$ relative to the main boundaries or center lines of the object.

q: 88. Horizontal lines are drawn
explain: Horizontal lines can technically be drawn either way, though standard practice for right-handed drafters is left-to-right.

q: 89. Vertical lines are drawn
explain: Vertical lines are drawn using a set square, moving either from top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top.

q: 90. The other name of axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection represents 3D objects on a single (one) plane of projection.

q: 91. One plane projection is
explain: Both Axonometric and Oblique projections create a 3D effect on a single projection plane.

q: 92. Axonometric view/drawing is what type of view?
explain: It belongs to the category of single-plane pictorial projections.

q: 93. Axonometric drawing is a drawing like
explain: In axonometric projection, the projectors are perpendicular (orthogonal) to the plane of projection.

q: 94. In one plane drawing, which one does not falls under
explain: Standard orthographic projection usually involves multiple planes (multi-view); axonometric, oblique, and dimetric are single-plane pictorials.

q: 95. A 100 m long line making 30 degree with the vertical, show its projection on horizontal plane
explain: Projection on HP = $L \times \sin(\theta)$ if angle is with vertical. $100 \times \sin(30^{\circ}) = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ m}$.

q: 96. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called
explain: The 'Origin' is the point where the X, Y (and Z) axes intersect ($0,0$).

q: 97. Axonometric projection is a special types of
explain: Axonometric is a sub-type of orthographic projection because the projectors are perpendicular to the plane.

q: 98. In case of dimetric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In Dimetric projection, two of the three axes are equally inclined to the plane of projection.

q: 99. In a topographic drawing the symbols representing natural features are drawn by free hand while artificial works are drawn by
explain: Man-made or artificial structures in maps (buildings, roads) are drawn with tools for precision, whereas natural features (coastlines, rivers) are often sketched.

q: 100. The symbol indicates
explain: The symbol showing a dome and a crescent/minaret is the standard cartographic representation for a Mosque.
